recognition: Limited formal diplomatic recognition alongside extensive unofficial relations. The PRC claim and Taiwan’s self-government must be represented separately.
provenance: Researched dossier. Each cited source has its own date; the newest citation is not a live verification of every field. No control geometry is inferred from areas of activity.
summary: Self-governing democracy administered by the Republic of China. The People’s Republic of China claims Taiwan, while the two governments maintain separate political and military institutions.
rulers: Lai Ching-te, elected president in January 2024; verified by CRS in August 2025.
economy: Export-oriented economy with a major role in semiconductor and technology supply chains.
military: Separate armed forces under ROC civilian authorities.
origin: The ROC government relocated to Taiwan after its defeat on mainland China in 1949; political liberalization followed in the late twentieth century.
contributions: Semiconductor manufacturing and global electronics supply chains.

sourceFields.military: Taiwan Armed Forces: Army, Navy (includes Marine Corps), Air Force, Information Communication and Electronic Force (ICEF) Ocean Affairs Council: Coast Guard Administration (CGA) Ministry of Interior: National Police (2025)
sourceFields.militaryNotes: note: the CGA is a law enforcement organization with homeland security functions during peacetime and national defense missions during wartime
sourceFields.economy: high-income East Asian economy; most technologically advanced computer microchip manufacturing; increasing Chinese interference threatens market capabilities; minimum wages rising; longstanding regional socioeconomic inequality
